title: Gmail service boundary
summary: The normal agent uses deterministic gmail. capabilities in tools.py. The model chooses searches, drafts text and interprets results; the adapters perform concrete provider operations.
html:
Gmail service boundary

The normal agent uses deterministic gmail.* capabilities in tools.py. The model chooses searches, drafts text and interprets results; the adapters perform concrete provider operations. Retrieved bodies, headers and attachment names remain untrusted external data.

flowchart TD Agent[Accepted Gmail tool invocation] --> Policy[Capability and confirmation policy] Policy --> Profiles[Current Parameter Store account and scopes] Profiles --> REST[OAuth: authorized REST client] Profiles --> Password[App password: request-bound adapter] REST --> Google[Gmail REST API] Password --> Gateway[Selected verified Gateway] Gateway --> IMAP[Gmail IMAP] Password --> Email[Shared Email SMTP pipeline] Email --> Gateway Gateway --> SMTP[Gmail SMTP] REST --> Result[Result or uncertain-effect evidence] Password --> Result Result --> Receipt[Existing native invocation receipt]

GmailService owns common live reads, MIME composition and the legacy preview/modify interface. Its authorized proxy creates the REST client, which calls Google from the controller using urllib; OAuth mail requests do not traverse the app-password Gateway adapter. Named compound actions have separate orchestration in client_actions.py and workflows.py.

gmail_app_password_account selects the request-scoped adapter in app_password.py. OAuth accounts keep the REST path. The adapter reuses Gmail MIME, artifact and bulk-preview logic and the private Email SMTP delivery/receipt pipeline. Gmail's capability policy owns Gmail sends independently of the Email skill. App passwords are unconditionally excluded from parameter projections, history, diagnostics and protocol logging.

gateway_core/gmail_runtime.py serves version-one private /gmail/operation requests on inbound and outbound Gateways. IMAPClient 3.x owns each request's verified TLS connection, inside the existing cancellable socket boundary. Literals, lines, aggregate MIME reads, cursor counts and private chunk transfers are bounded. Transfers are invocation-owned; cursors bind account revision, query, run and mailbox UIDVALIDITY, and expire after ten minutes. Both stores are volatile and discarded on process restart. No controller IMAP/SMTP fallback exists.

The Gateway runtime has separate 100-entry cursor and transfer stores. Cursor snapshots share a 100,000-row ceiling; each listing allows at most 50,000 unique results. Continuation consumes the token before checking saved UIDVALIDITY, and a new page token gets its own ten-minute expiry. Account, run, method and query options bind the cursor; page size may change between requests. Private transfers allow 40 MiB per blob and 96 MiB of declared staging capacity, with 48-KiB chunks and SHA-256 verification. Cancellation discards the run's cursors and the invocation's transfers before requesting socket cancellation.

gmail_imap.py bounds each IMAP line to one MiB and each literal to 25 MiB, with a 40-MiB protocol receive budget reset per fetch. Decoded MIME bytes have a separate 25-MiB aggregate budget across message reads in one mailbox request. MIME conversion rejects depth above 50 or more than 2,000 parts. These limits can reject a large result before the controller applies text clipping.

Gmail extensions provide hexadecimal message/thread IDs and labels; special-use folder attributes locate localized mailboxes. Reads use BODY.PEEK, archive removes the Inbox label, and cross-folder trash transitions require UID MOVE. Explicit permanent deletion uses BulkMailbox.change: require UIDPLUS, move only the selected messages to Trash when necessary, resolve their current UIDs again, set Deleted on those UIDs and issue targeted UID EXPUNGE. Moving from another folder also requires MOVE; messages already in Trash need no MOVE capability. Unrestricted EXPUNGE, expunging CLOSE and implicit account-wide deletion-setting changes are not used. Draft replacement verifies a new APPENDUID before cleanup and checks the old draft's content identity and draft/sent state again. Confirmed substeps are checkpointed in the existing native invocation receipt before dependent operations. Restart preserves those facts while an unfinished operation remains unknown and cannot be replayed.

AgentParameterStore is the sole durable owner of OAuth app configuration and account/token bundles. parameters/templates.py defines gmail_oauth_app and gmail_account, validates their version-one contracts and projects safe identities. skills/gmail/parameter_profiles.py resolves canonical keys and updates the existing account record after token exchange or refresh. Accepted private references supply account identity; Gmail resolves the current record for token lifecycle, rename and deletion behavior.

auth/gmail_compat.py retains the legacy Gmail adapter; auth/browser.py owns the common browser/PKCE lifecycle and auth/google/client.py owns shared Google/Gmail refresh; skills/gmail/oauth.py is a compatibility import. The adapter holds ten-minute OAuth state and PKCE verifiers only in process memory. Desktop authorization uses a temporary loopback listener; web applications use their configured controller callback. State is consumed once before exchange, and the Gmail profile supplies the authenticated email. Browser launch failure leaves a usable consent URL. Refreshes share process-wide account locks, retain an omitted refresh token and never silently select another account. Provider 401 rejection permits one refresh attempt. Reads have bounded retry for throttling/transient server errors; writes are never blindly retried after an uncertain response.

There are no runtime Gmail account tables, mailbox tables, body caches, indexes, labels/draft mirrors, attachment caches, OAuth-state tables, or sync/watch managers. Gmail authorization is created directly in Parameter Store through the current OAuth flow. The old Gmail database, secret key and configuration importer are absent. Old files are never imported, renamed or deleted by startup. gmail/store.py, gmail/sync.py, and gmail/broker.py remain removed.

Mail reads return bounded projections into normal task/model context. Search retrieves at most 100 metadata summaries per page, reports individual header-read failures and leaves attachment presence unknown. Message text defaults to 20,000 characters; REST thread detail retains the last 100 messages under a shared 40,000-character body budget and at most 100 attachment summaries. An app-password direct thread read rejects more than 100 messages before fetching their bodies; compound state selection can expand threads up to its separate 50,000-ID ceiling. The compatibility refresh arguments do not select a cache: reads still query the provider. Full resources are used for explicit reads, reply/forward construction and attachment lookup.

These projection limits are not ordinary REST response-byte limits. Individual REST requests read and decode the whole HTTP body before MIME projection and use a 45-second socket timeout, not an overall operation deadline. The separate REST multipart helper accepts at most 50 parts and caps the response at 40 MiB; Gateway IMAP has its own protocol and transfer bounds. The full-message header projection has no local count/value cap; the separate read_headers action caps 100 entries and 20,000 combined characters. mime.py extracts plain text from HTML for context; this does not make the original HTML safe to render.

Tool observations follow the normal task lifecycle; there is no separate persistent mailbox. files.py publishes explicit downloads as sensitive run artifacts. Outgoing Context/artifact references require existing conversation access and share a 25-MiB byte ceiling; temporary paths pass through the ordinary publication mechanism before reading.

Legacy preview_modify selections contain account identity, operation, label name, IDs, hash and timestamps in process memory. They share a pool of at most 100 active selections with compound-action approval snapshots. App-password previews additionally bind mailbox identity and run. Tokens are one-use and expire after ten minutes; execution validates the selection and consumes its token before resolving label changes or writing. A later failure does not restore the token. The returned ID display is capped at 100, independently of selection completeness. An incomplete legacy preview can still describe a bounded subset, so callers must inspect truncated; named compound actions enforce their own all-or-limit contract. Native REST batchModify chunks contain at most 1,000 IDs; the app-password adapter groups changes in batches of 500. No Gmail plan database exists. After restart, preview again. See compound mailbox changes.

Generic execution receipts, confirmation grants and replay guards remain authoritative. Ambiguous sends/mutations raise UnknownEffectError. Outgoing messages carry an RFC822 Message-ID. Following a lost send response, one exact Sent match can reconcile the send; otherwise the operation remains unknown and is not repeated. A Sent match does not prove recipient delivery. Receipts belong to the existing RunStore, not a Gmail send database.

checkpoint.py merges allowlisted confirmed substeps into that existing invocation claim before dependent work. RAM and standalone SQLite adapters use their transaction boundaries; an invocation without a supplied receipt store has only object-local checkpoint state. Message bodies and credentials are excluded from checkpoint fields. A confirmed SMTP acceptance survives draft-cleanup failure, and a reconciled Sent match can still leave recipient acceptance unconfirmed. Both facts remain explicit in the result rather than triggering another send.

Parameter Store UI templates and the existing mention palette provide configuration and account selection. The retained Gmail HTTP routes call the shared service directly: writes require EULA acceptance, bulk POST supplies explicit confirmation, and uncertain effects map to HTTP 409. These routes do not construct native invocation receipts, run artifact context or the app-password Gateway adapter. Use the native Gmail tools for those workflows. Retired cache/config routes return 410. No Gmail-specific model, email-client UI, secure vault, encryption system or notification architecture is introduced.

Provider contracts follow Gmail REST reference, native OAuth with PKCE, and Gmail scopes.

Neutral google_account profiles are optional Gmail identities. The shared resolver in auth/google/accounts.py considers eligible legacy and neutral records together. Gmail scope_requirements.py checks each neutral operation, including internal provider calls; legacy provider scope/error semantics remain stable. Native accepted references and explicit account keys select exact identities. Gmail sends, uncertain effects, MIME and public tool IDs retain their existing behavior. See Google Workspace foundation for schemas and reuse by Calendar/Drive.
